source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check ME FW error code is normal.
1. Check the information of test item

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. Information should be correct and still be correct after rebooting

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: ls /sys/class/mei/ 2>&1; echo ---; mei-amt-check -E 2>&1 || echo "ME FW Error Code tool not installed"; echo ---; dmesg | grep -iE "error|me.fw" | tail -20
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: read the ME error code (ME FW Error Code) via the MEI/SPS channel. The agent collects whatever MEI/SPS registers/dmesg lines are reachable; confirming the value is CORRECT requires knowing the expected value (a user-supplied baseline), so this is PARTIAL: agent returns the raw readout, user judges it against the expected ME FW Error Code.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: read-only attempt against Intel MEI/SPS registers using vendor tools (intelmetool / mei-amt-check) that may not be installed on the SUT; install/availability must be confirmed first, and the expected baseline value must be provided by the user.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL; identifies the missing expected code but does not verify whether -E only reads or could acknowledge/clear faults, and omits post-reboot collection.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED; requires vendor decoder, acceptable state, non-clearing tool and preserved pre/post evidence.
historical_reviews.round_02: PARTIAL; collects generic error evidence but does not distinguish authoritative ME code from unrelated dmesg errors.
historical_reviews.second_review_handoff: Confirms existing error evidence must never be cleared and a platform decoder is required.

original_test_intent: Read the platform-specific ME firmware error code without clearing or acknowledging it, decode it against the owner-defined acceptable/no-error state and verify the preserved state remains correct after an approved reboot.
original_method: Use a documented read-only, non-clearing ME error-code query to capture raw code and vendor decode before reboot; perform one approved controlled reboot, repeat the same query and compare both results while preserving all related logs.
manual_activity: The authorized user supplies the decoder/acceptable state, validates that the query cannot clear or acknowledge errors, approves the reboot and later issues the verdict. The full acquisition and comparison sequence is electronic and automatable.
required_inputs: Exact platform/SKU and ME/SPS firmware generation
Vendor error-code table plus acceptable raw code/mask/state
Approved read-only and non-clearing MEI utility/version/exact syntax
Maintenance approval, reboot/reconnect timeout and OOB recovery
safety_requirements: Never clear, acknowledge, reset or remediate an ME error as part of the check.
Do not equate generic kernel errors with the authoritative ME firmware error code.
Preserve pre-existing MEI, kernel, BMC and SEL evidence and approve the reboot before affecting availability.
Stop on tool side effects, unknown code layout, code change, query failure or recovery anomaly; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Validate the decoder and non-clearing query, inventory platform/ME identity and capture raw/decoded pre-reboot code plus related evidence.
Perform one approved controlled reboot and track downtime/reconnect without altering ME state.
Repeat the identical query, compare expected/pre/post codes and correlate kernel/BMC/SEL evidence without assigning PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Provide the authoritative error-code semantics/acceptable state and certify the diagnostic is read-only/non-clearing.
Approve the reboot and recovery plan.
Review preserved fault evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: sysfs and dmesg are supporting diagnostics only. mei-amt-check -E must be proven non-clearing and platform-valid; the broad error grep is not the ME code and the sequence lacks the post-reboot read.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the approved non-clearing vendor ME error-code query and retain exact raw output and decode before and after one approved reboot.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: ME FW Error Code normality, persistence after reboot and 5/0-minute fields are preserved; existing error evidence is not sanitized.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Capture a structured raw ME error code, vendor decode, platform identity and related persistent evidence with the identical non-clearing query before and after reboot.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the ME/SPS generation covered by the supplied error-code table and diagnostic.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record ME/SPS firmware, BIOS, MEI driver, diagnostic utility, OS and kernel.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Use platform/vendor ME error-code and diagnostic documentation supplied for this target.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Defines non-clearing behavior, code semantics and the omitted post-reboot comparison.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; acceptable code and persistence are both retained while fault history is preserved.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Error-code decoder, acceptable state and certified non-clearing query.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Some codes may be sticky, historical or boot-phase dependent; the owner must define how those states are evaluated without clearing them.

project_override_considerations: A project defines acceptable/sticky code semantics and the reboot plan. Missing definitions delay readiness but do not reduce full automation capability; project policy must not authorize clearing evidence within this case.
expected_evidence: Platform/SKU, ME/SPS/BIOS/MEI identity and non-clearing query-tool manifest
Vendor code table and owner-approved acceptable/sticky-code rule
Raw/decoded pre-reboot error code, preserved related logs, approved reboot/downtime/reconnect transcript and raw/decoded post-reboot code
Code comparison, proof no clear/reset occurred, BMC/SEL/kernel health, Tool Result and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Normal error-code state and correctness after reboot are compatible. Undefined code semantics and tooling are readiness inputs, not contradictory source facts.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The intended error-code read/persistence check is clear. Missing decoder/tool/reboot parameters do not create permanent BLOCKED, and all core steps can be automated after approval.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains its baseline/tool caveat but rejects the generic grep and PARTIAL capability label.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its non-clearing, decoder and reboot safeguards while reclassifying to FULLY AUTOMATABLE under V3.1 readiness separation.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Explicitly protects sticky/pre-existing error evidence and separates raw code, decode, Tool Result and verdict.

review_improvement: Prevents a diagnostic from hiding the very error under test, provides auditable pre/post code evidence and avoids treating expert interpretation as a manual execution requirement.
independent_technical_reasoning: A verified non-clearing code query, reboot and repeat query are automatable. The owner-supplied decoder and final interpretation affect readiness and verdict only, so capability is FULLY AUTOMATABLE.
